lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Taking Care of My Own Space
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: the five-minute tidy

objective: Learners follow a four-step five-minute tidy routine (pick up floor items, clear the flat surfaces, put items back where they belong, do one last visual scan) in their own bedroom or a shared space, timing themselves so they learn what a five-minute effort actually looks like.
scenario: The learner picks one small, real space, such as their bedroom floor or a corner of a shared playroom, sets a timer for five minutes, and runs through the four-step routine once while a family member is nearby but not doing the tidying for them.
materials: one real space that needs tidying

tasks.directions: Before starting the timer, look at your space and picture how it will look when you are done.

prompts.text: Name the one spot in your space that looks the messiest right now.

tasks.directions: Set a timer for five minutes and run the four steps in order: pick up floor items, clear flat surfaces, put items back where they belong, then do one last visual scan.

prompts.text: I picked up every item on the floor first, before touching surfaces.
I cleared off at least one flat surface, like a desk or dresser top.
I put items back in a specific home, not just a different pile.
I did one last visual scan of the whole space before stopping the timer.
Did you finish all four steps before the timer ran out, or did you need more time? If you needed more time, which step took longest?

tasks.directions: Compare your space to how it looked before.

prompts.text: Describe one specific difference between your space before and after the five-minute tidy.

remediation: If a learner runs out of time on step one because they stop to play with items they pick up, reteach with a one-handed rule: the picking-up hand only carries items to their home and does not stop to use them, practiced on five scattered items before returning to the full space.
extension: Have the learner run the same five-minute tidy in a second space the next day and compare, in writing, which of the two spaces was faster to tidy and why.
